chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Samāʿah, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Allah does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then take it away from him unless he commits a sin by which he deserves that removal.”

key_terms.فَسَلَبَهَا: then took it away or removed it
key_terms.نِعْمَةً: a divine blessing or bounty granted to a servant

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah remove blessings from a person according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the removal of a divine blessing is not arbitrary, but is connected to a servant’s sinful conduct. It highlights divine justice and warns that sin can become the cause for losing the favors Allah has granted.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Sama’at who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Favour upon a servant by a bounty then He<sup>azwj</sup> Confiscates it from him, unless he commits a sin to be deserving of that Confiscation’.
en.sarwar: 24. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Sama’a who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah does not take away the favor that He grants to a servant as long as he does not commit a sin that may subject him to losing Allah’s favor.’”
